verdict.rationale: Turso's docs describe the story directly: you can provision a dedicated, isolated SQLite database per user or AI agent, token-scope it, and tear it down via the API (turso-docs-8). The Platform API manages databases, groups, organizations and tokens programmatically (turso-docs-60), and the marketing claims you can spin up thousands or millions of isolated databases (turso-docs-12, turso-docs-48). Per-preview databases are covered by automated branching for each pull request (turso-docs-11, turso-docs-18), with per-database token restrictions and MCP- and CLI-based fleet management (turso-docs-56, turso-docs-37, turso-docs-50). Missing for 10: concrete pricing or limit evidence showing per-database cost at thousands-scale (only one anecdotal 'cheap, free tier' comment), and independent or hands-on corroboration of large fleet sizes.
